clue.text: Rejected really foolish request for material

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word for foolish is read backwards

parts.note: really foolish means mad
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an absurd demand for some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, often of silk or linen, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Barb beginning to enjoy most of alcoholic drink

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark, a dig

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of enjoy
most of means the last letter is dropped from the word for alcoholic

parts.note: a stiff drink is a strong alcoholic one

explanation.surface: A sharp remark starts the fun over a strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A digestif is an alcoholic drink such as brandy taken after a meal to aid digestion.

clue.text: Stones from mass shrine all over the place

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stones from a big holy site are scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Menhirs are tall upright prehistoric standing stones.

clue.text: Elegant parts of ships hoisted

indicators.note: hoisted means raised, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: keels are the bottom structures of ships

explanation.surface: Graceful sections of vessels are lifted from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and stylish in line, so elegant in appearance.

clue.text: "Au revoir" from sailor regularly given no rum?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words given no, starting with the second

parts.note: the even letters of these two words
a tot is a small measure of rum

explanation.surface: A sailor bids farewell having been refused his rum ration.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'no' is fodder, not a refusal: the even letters of 'given no' supply the middle of the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bientot is French for 'see you soon', a farewell phrase much like au revoir.

clue.text: Claret-covered minor celeb makes complaint

indicators.note: covered means one piece sits on top of the other in this down entry

parts.note: claret is old boxing slang for blood
a B-lister is a second-rank celebrity

explanation.surface: A lesser star, spattered with red wine, grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood blister is a minor medical complaint, a skin swelling filled with blood.

clue.text: Writer in Australia packing beer and fruit when climbing

indicators.note: climbing means going up, so in this down entry the whole is read upwards
packing means one word is stuffed into the other: the word for Australia goes into the word for beer

parts.note: ale is beer
Oz is a nickname for Australia
a lime is a fruit

explanation.surface: An author in Australia loads up on beer and fruit while hiking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' covers the whole of the wordplay, the container and the fruit together, since this is a down entry read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was the French novelist who wrote Germinal and J'accuse.

clue.text: Relieved when husband leaves maximum amount of fuel

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for husband departs from the word for relieved

parts.note: relieved means thankful

explanation.surface: A wife is relieved when her husband sets off with a full tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankful is as much as a fuel tank holds, so the most a car can take.

clue.text: Note outside of church: 'No Dance Music'

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: outside of means the outer letters of church

explanation.surface: A notice pinned on a church bans dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music with a fast repetitive beat.

clue.text: Pig and shrew overturned trap

indicators.note: overturned means the word for shrew is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a shrew is a nagging woman, a nag
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A pig and a shrew have tipped over a trap they were caught in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' and 'shrew' both look like animals, but 'Pig' is the definition and 'shrew' a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gannet is slang for a greedy eater, just as a pig is someone who gobbles food.

clue.text: A difficult situation perhaps for teddy bears

definitions.text: A difficult situation perhaps for teddy bears

parts.words: A difficult situation perhaps for teddy bears
parts.note: alludes to the song The Teddy Bears' Picnic; an idiom for something hard is said to be no outing in the park

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for something hard literally describes the absence of the teddy bears' famous outing from the children's song.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no picnic' describes a task or situation that is hard or unpleasant.

clue.text: Crowded House maybe playing a stage in Rome

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters perform in a new order

explanation.surface: The band Crowded House are performing on a stage in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Crowded House is a pop band, but here it is a household made crowded by three.
explanation.definitionFit: A menage a trois is a three-person household or relationship; three is famously a crowd.

clue.text: Unfortunate demise of arachnid yankee put in post

indicators.note: put in means the arachnid and yankee letters are placed inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tick is an arachnid, related to mites and spiders
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A spider and an American are posted off to a grim fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to a sticky end is an idiom for meeting an unpleasant death.

clue.text: Charming the Spanish end using another language

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
fin is French for end

explanation.surface: Finishing a sentence in a foreign tongue makes it sound charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something delicate and enchanting, like a fairy, so it can mean charming.

clue.text: Pluto? Fancy meeting you here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Pluto, demoted to a dwarf planet, is a small world
second meaning: what people say when bumping into an acquaintance in an unexpected place

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the first reading as cryptic: the phrase literally describes the dwarf planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock remark on a chance meeting with an acquaintance far from home is this phrase about coincidence.

clue.text: Excellent member of parliament makes US championship

parts.note: superb means excellent
a group of owls is called a parliament, so an owl is a member

explanation.surface: An outstanding MP wins an American title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member of parliament' wants to be an MP; it is a bird, since a parliament is a flock of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the annual championship game of American football's NFL.

clue.text: Cut short series college held in gallery

indicators.note: held in means these letters are contained by the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
a run is a series

explanation.surface: A run of college exhibitions at a gallery is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten something by cutting off a part.

clue.text: Youth's cat perhaps primarily prefers eating raw fish

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a kind of whip

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a snapper is a fish

explanation.surface: A young person's cat likes to dine on raw fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth's' is 'Youth is', the definition then a link. The first letters of 'prefers eating raw' give PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impertinent young person, so a youth.

clue.text: Rash is treated with a spicy paste

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: A skin rash is soothed with a hot condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste.

clue.text: Old Haitian in M*A*S*H carried by American medic

indicators.note: carried by means this piece rests on the following ones in this down entry

parts.note: mash, pulped food, is pap
a doc is a doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A Haitian appears in the TV comedy M*A*S*H, played by a US army doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisks dress mash up as the Korean War TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa Doc was the nickname of Francois Duvalier, dictator of Haiti until 1971.

clue.text: 17s fiddle on deserted promenades

parts.note: a fiddle is a scam, a swindle

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, so only the outer letters of promenades remain

explanation.surface: Young rascals run a swindle on the empty seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous children, impudent young people like whippersnappers.

clue.text: One who helps another European to quit job

indicators.note: to quit means the European letter leaves the word for job

parts.note: a career is a job

explanation.surface: A European is helped to leave their employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after a sick, elderly or disabled person, helping someone else.

clue.text: Hot puree not cooked at that point

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone notices their hot puree has not been cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon means immediately after that, at that moment.

clue.text: Misgiving briefly after English match

indicators.note: after means the English letter comes first, with the next piece following it
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a qualm is a misgiving

explanation.surface: A brief doubt follows an English football game.
explanation.definitionFit: To equal something is to match it, to be its peer.

clue.text: Extinct animal linking llamas to donkeys

indicators.note: linking means the answer runs across the join of these words

explanation.surface: A prehistoric beast forms an evolutionary link between llamas and donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was an elephant-like mammal that died out thousands of years ago.

clue.text: Cold plain cask mild punter finally accepted

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: finally means taking the last letter of each of the words mild and punter

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: A pub-goer finally takes a cask of mild beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mild' looks like the beer in the cask, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless Arctic region where the subsoil stays frozen.

clue.text: Go alongside the French road that's most secure

parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab
le is French for the
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Travelling beside a French road is the safest choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stablest is the superlative of stable, meaning firmest and least likely to fall.

clue.text: Covering exposed acer conserves water

indicators.note: conserves means the inner letters hold the word for water inside them
exposed means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the inside of acer

parts.note: a loch is a lake, a body of water

explanation.surface: A gardener's maple tree, left uncovered, keeps hold of rainwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a glass or plastic cover put over young plants to protect them.
